title: Does Financial System Stability Foster  Sustainability? Evidence from European  Union Countries
content: Financial stability may support investment and employment, yet environmental and social progress may respond differently. This study examines how bank capital adequacy, loan portfolio quality and financial market stress relate to renewable energy, per-capita greenhouse gas emissions and employment across European Union countries. Using unbalanced panels for 2010–2024 and 2015–2024, we estimate models with country and year fixed effects; common-sample comparisons and a composite sustain-ability index are exploratory. In the primary 26-country financial-stress panel, a 0.1-point higher stress index was associated with a 0.305 percentage-point smaller annual change in the employment rate. Still, the association was not statistically significant after adjustment for three outcomes. Environmental estimates and primary bank-capital estimates were uncertain, and inference methods disagreed for installed wind capacity. Exploratory models with outcome-specific controls retained a negative stress–employment association, although its statistical significance depended on the scope of multiple-testing adjustment. The composite index reflected this pattern mainly through employment. These findings highlight a recurring association between financial stress and employment and show why environmental and social outcomes should be assessed separately.
